title: In Silico Study of Mercury Resistance Genes Extracted from Pseudomonas spp. Involved in Bioremediation: Understanding the Promoter Regions and Regulatory Elements.
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习方法分析假单胞菌汞抗性基因启动子区的转录因子结合基序与调控元件，虽涉及TF-DNA结合位点预测，但对象为原核生物启动子调控，非典型真核TF-DNA互作体系，且缺乏三维结构建模与动态机制研究。
abstract: Microbial genes and their product were diverse and beneficial for heavy metal bioremediation from the contaminated sites. Screening of genes and gene products plays a significant role in the detoxification of pollutants. Understanding of the promoter region and its regulatory elements is a vital implication of microbial genes. To the best of our knowledge, there is no in silico study reported so far on mer gene families used for heavy metal bioremediation. The motif distribution was observed densely upstream of the TSSs (transcription start sites) between +1 and -350 bp and sparsely distributed above -350 bp, according to the current study. MEME identified the best common candidate motifs of TFs (transcription factors) binding with the lowest e value (7.2e-033) and is the most statistically significant candidate motif. The EXPREG output of the 11 TFs with varying degrees of function such as activation, repression, transcription, and dual purposes was thoroughly examined. Data revealed that transcriptional gene regulation in terms of activation and repression was observed at 36.4% and 54.56%, respectively. This shows that most TFs are involved in transcription gene repression rather than activation. Likewise, EXPREG output revealed that transcriptional conformational modes, such as monomers, dimers, tetramers, and other factors, were also analyzed. The data indicated that most of the transcriptional conformation mode was dual, which accounts for 96%. CpG island analysis using online and offline tools revealed that the gene body had fewer CpG islands compared to the promoter regions. Understanding the common candidate motifs, transcriptional factors, and regulatory elements of the mer operon gene cluster using a machine learning approach could help us better understand gene expression patterns in heavy metal bioremediation.
abstract_zh: 微生物基因及其产物具有多样性，并对受污染场地的重金属生物修复具有益处。基因及基因产物的筛选在污染物解毒中发挥着重要作用。理解启动子区域及其调控元件是微生物基因功能的重要方面。据我们所知，目前尚无关于用于重金属生物修复的mer基因家族的计算模拟研究报告。根据本研究，基序分布密集地位于TSSs（转录起始位点）上游+1至-350 bp区域，而在-350 bp以上则分布稀疏。MEME识别出最佳的常见候选转录因子（TFs）结合基序，其e值最低（7.2e-033），且为统计上最显著的候选基序。对11个转录因子具有不同程度功能（如激活、抑制、转录及双重作用）的EXPREG输出进行了全面检查。数据显示，转录基因调控中激活和抑制分别占36.4%和54.56%。这表明大多数转录因子参与转录基因抑制而非激活。同样，EXPREG输出显示，转录构象模式，如单体、二聚体、四聚体及其他因子，也进行了分析。数据表明，大多数转录构象模式为双重模式，占96%。使用在线和离线工具进行的CpG岛分析显示，基因体中的CpG岛数量少于启动子区域。通过机器学习方法理解mer操纵子基因簇的常见候选基序、转录因子及调控元件，有助于我们更好地理解重金属生物修复中的基因表达模式。
